alignments.note: Rule 66: 'man' is the generic completion of νεανίσκος and 'young' carries the sense, as πλεονέκτης → 'covetous man' heads on 'covetous'. Heading on 'man' is defensible.
συνακολουθέω → 'followed'. The σύν- prefix is not a source token of its own; the English 'with' answers to the government of the dative αὐτῷ and stays outside this unit.

Rules 21 and 36: the case preposition realizing the dative rides with the pronoun, as at MRK.14.5, 14.46, 14.53 and 14.65 and as rule 69's οὐ κατενάρκησα οὐθενός → 'on any man' does for a compound verb. MRK.14.54's plain ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ → 'followed him' is the evidence for the competing reading, which gives 'with' to the verb's σύν- element.
Rule 15: 'having … cast about him' is discontinuous around the object noun phrase; the reflexive object is a rule 7 pronoun helper.
Rule 51's anarthrous clause; 'linen cloth' glosses σινδών, headed on the noun.
Rule 17's generic-noun clause: with anarthrous Greek the substantival adjective takes the supplied possessive and noun, headed on the adjective.

Rule 17: 'lay hold on' heads on the meaning-bearing complement. 'on' stays with the verb because αὐτόν is accusative and English needs no case preposition for a direct object; contrast the dative αὐτῷ earlier in this verse, where the preposition realizes the case and rides with the pronoun.

review_notes: Two units changed: συνηκολούθει and the dative αὐτῷ beside it. Everything else is as the verse pass returned it.
MRK.14.54's plain ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ -> 'followed him' shows the ASV rendering the same dative bare; that is the evidence for the competing reading and it is named in the note.
κρατοῦσιν αὐτόν keeps 'lay hold on' whole because αὐτόν is accusative, and its note now says so.
